name: draw_line_pixels_planes
description: Plots a one-pixel line into the four-plane bitmap by setting the pixel bit in each plane for every step. It steps along the longer axis and advances the other axis on an error counter, with direction flags deciding the sign of each step.

name: draw_pixel_column_planes
description: Sets one pixel bit in each of the four bitplanes for a vertical run of pixels, moving down by the row stride once per pixel. The starting position comes from the screen origin variables and the count from a data register.

name: draw_pixel_column_at_pointer
description: Sets one pixel bit in each of the four bitplanes at a pointer passed in a register, then steps the pointer by a row stride for the count given. Bit index and stride are passed in registers.

name: draw_sloped_line_planes
description: Draws a sloped line in the four bitplanes by stepping along the major axis and advancing the minor axis on an error term started at half the major length. Start coordinates are taken from the screen origin variables.

name: draw_line_from_pointer_planes
description: Draws a Bresenham-style line from a pointer into the four bitplanes, with the error term, bit index and row stride supplied in registers. Each step sets the pixel in all four planes and moves to the next bit or byte column.

name: fill_span_planes_pattern
description: Fills a horizontal span of pixels across the four bitplanes by setting single bits at the ragged ends and writing whole bytes of per-plane pattern values for full eight-pixel groups. Pattern bytes are read from the global data block.

name: fill_span_from_pointer_planes
description: Sets pixel bits across a horizontal span in the four bitplanes, starting from a pointer and bit index in registers. It writes whole eight-pixel groups as bit operations and moves to the next row with the stride register.

name: draw_wide_slope_line_planes
description: Draws a line with a shallow slope in the four bitplanes using nested loops, where the inner loop sets pixels along a byte run and the outer loop steps rows. The error term is halved from the start width before the loop.

name: draw_slope_line_pointer_planes
description: Draws a line from a pointer into the four bitplanes using nested loops, setting the same pixel bit in each plane and advancing the error counter for each step. The stride and error values arrive in registers.

name: store_point_then_call_draw
description: Copies two 16-bit values from the argument into fixed slots of the global data block and then calls another routine. Pointers in the data hunk reference it as an entry point.

name: store_point_call_and_return
description: Copies the two 16-bit halves of its argument into fixed global slots, calls another routine, and returns the data registers as they stand after that call. It is entered through a handler pointer in the data hunk.

name: plot_pixel_in_clip_rect
description: Plots one pixel in the four bitplanes only when its x and y coordinates lie inside a rectangle held as four global limits. The y value is offset by a base row and the x value by a base column before the bit is set.

name: plot_pixel_at_pointer
description: Sets one pixel bit in each of the four bitplanes at the address and bit index given in registers. It is called directly from the line and span routines without a bounds check.

name: clear_bitmap_block_longwords
description: Writes zero longwords backwards from a computed start address in an unrolled store loop. The start address is derived from a row offset in the global data block and the screen base, clearing a block of bitmap rows.

name: draw_scaled_coordinate_sequence
description: Divides table entries and a computed value to produce scaled coordinates, then passes them through a sequence of indirect calls. The sequence repeats for 29 and then 18 entries, with a fixed divisor of -10000 used for one call.

name: project_and_plot_point_table
description: Processes up to 24 groups of four 16-bit points, scaling each by a 512-based divisor with a fixed 600 offset and writing six derived values per group to a table. A second pass combines pairs of table values and plots those inside the clip range.

name: draw_select_menu_labels
description: Places a sequence of text labels at fixed screen positions, including the level select prompt, the easy, medium and hard options, the bonus choices, and the wave and point entries. It then clears two state variables.

name: update_countdown_and_input_modes
description: Updates a countdown digit from a frame counter divided by 50 and advances a second counter. It then reads an input value several times against 15 and sets one of three mode values that each call a block of drawing routines; otherwise it draws a fixed set of shapes.

name: run_title_wait_loop
description: Draws the prompt text 'or wait for info, pull trigger to start' and loops a three-state dispatcher until its state reaches 3. Between dispatch steps it draws two text blocks and copies two areas of the bitmap.

name: wait_for_input_or_timeout
description: Runs a per-frame loop for up to 500 frames until a state variable becomes nonzero, calling four routines each frame. If the state is still zero at the end it clears a flag and returns all ones; otherwise it returns whether the state is not four.

name: build_scaled_point_table
description: Fills a 128-entry table with paired values taken from a source table, shifting one value by five and deriving the others through a conversion routine with offsets of 100 and 2000. It then sets two global limits and calls another routine.

name: draw_credits_text_lines
description: Draws the credit lines 'German voices digitized from', '1988', 'The System Breaker' and 'STAR WARS' at offsets from a base row. It then calls a block copy routine for a fixed area of the bitmap.

name: draw_intro_text_block
description: Draws eight lines of story text at increasing row offsets, including the Death Star and Force lines, then calls a block copy routine for the text area. The strings are referenced directly from the routine.

name: examine_undecompiled_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available for this 47-instruction routine. It has two callers and no listed callees or text, so its behaviour cannot be stated from the evidence.

name: update_star_field_positions
description: Advances 128 three-word star records by per-frame speed values derived from a lookup of the scaled input and adds offsets to their positions. It also increments a timer by two when the input is above ten and has its low two bits set.

name: inspect_timed_out_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available for this 30-instruction routine. It has one caller and no listed callees or text, so its behaviour cannot be stated from the evidence.

name: plot_indexed_coordinate_pairs
description: Reads pairs of 16-bit coordinates from a table at fixed indices and passes each one, offset by a global value, to two indirect routines. The calls cover a long fixed list of table entries, after which it draws the table's remaining points.

name: run_timed_sprite_sequence
description: Runs three frame-synchronised passes that step a changing value through a drawing routine: one from 100 down to minus 200, one from minus 50 up to 200 with a scaled value, and one from 100 down to minus 370. It returns the abort value when one is set, otherwise zero.

name: select_next_game_state
description: Returns the next state code from a frame counter, a flag and an argument. It returns 1 in the first 20 frames unless the argument is 1, clears the flag and returns 3 when the flag is set, and otherwise returns 0 or 2, after first passing any pending value to a routine.

name: update_particle_records_random
description: Advances 70 particle records by their velocities and respawns any that cross a boundary with random position and speed values. The sign of the argument selects which axis is updated, and each record is drawn after its update.

name: initialize_particle_records
description: Fills 70 three-word particle records with random starting positions taken from the high byte of two random values. Each record's third word is a random speed from 1 to 8.

name: draw_instruction_line_by_index
description: Selects one of about a dozen instruction text lines by a numeric index and draws it at a row offset from a base row. The screen base is pointed at a global buffer first, and the text covers X-Wing deflector, laser tower and fireball advice.

name: draw_scoring_table_text
description: Draws a scoring table with labels for Tie Fighters, Laser Towers, Trench Turrets, the Exhaust Port and the Darth Vader Ship, with point values from 1,000 to 50,000. It places the lines at fixed row offsets and then calls a block copy routine.

name: run_timed_scroll_sequence_a
description: Runs a 768-frame loop that waits for each frame tick and draws a column sequence every step. After frame 720 it reduces the scroll value by 256 every fifth step, and it returns the abort value when one is set.

name: run_timed_scroll_sequence_b
description: Runs the same 768-frame timed scroll loop as its neighbour, drawing a column sequence per step and reducing the scroll value by 256 after frame 720. It returns the abort value set during the loop.

name: run_timed_descent_sequence
description: Runs a frame-synchronised loop that counts down from 110 to minus 360 and draws a routine on each step while the scroll value is positive. Once the counter drops below minus 300, the scroll value is reduced by 257 every fifth step, and the abort value is returned.

name: store_table_word_by_nibble
description: Writes the second argument word into a 16-entry word table in the global block, indexed by the low four bits of the first argument.

name: wait_for_frame_count
description: Clears a frame counter and spins until it reaches the given count, so the caller waits for that many frame ticks.

name: compute_integer_square_root
description: Computes the integer square root of its argument with Newton iterations, starting from the argument divided by 200 plus two. It returns once successive estimates stop changing.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Contains only a return instruction and does nothing. Its one caller therefore has no effect from this routine.

name: set_default_bounds_fifteen
description: Stores 15, minus 15 and 15 into three global 16-bit variables with no other effect. The values are fixed constants.

name: set_window_limits_constants
description: Stores six fixed 16-bit constants into global variables: 160, 115, minus 160, 159, minus 84 and 84. Nothing in the routine names them.

name: scroll_depth_records_and_draw
description: Moves 31 three-word records by a scroll value, wrapping each record by adding or subtracting 14500 when it passes a limit. Each record is drawn through a routine, and a threshold check decides whether a second drawing routine is also called.

name: scroll_records_wrap_draw_loop
description: Loops over a count of three-word records supplied in registers, moving each by a step and wrapping it by 14500 when it falls below minus 500. Each record is then drawn, with the threshold check selecting a second drawing routine.

name: scroll_depth_records_forward
description: Moves 31 three-word records by a scroll value, wrapping each one by adding 14500 when it passes the upper limit. Each record is drawn through a routine, and a threshold check decides whether a second routine is also called.

name: scroll_depth_records_counted
description: Moves a counted run of three-word records by a scroll value and wraps each one by 14500 at the upper limit. Each record is drawn, with the threshold check selecting a second drawing routine.

name: update_starfield_with_motion
description: Moves 31 starfield records in depth, negating their lateral speeds when they wrap. For a positive argument it also shifts each lateral position by a scaled global velocity, keeping it in a 12-bit range, before drawing each record.

name: drift_records_wrapped_twelve_bit
description: Moves a counted run of records in depth and applies fixed lateral offsets, wrapping each lateral coordinate into a 12-bit range centred on zero. Records past the depth limit are repositioned and have their lateral speeds negated before drawing.

name: scroll_depth_records_mirror_wrap
description: Moves 31 three-word records by a scroll value and draws each one. Records that pass the upper limit are wrapped by 14500 and have their lateral speeds negated.

name: scroll_depth_records_counted_mirror
description: Moves a counted run of three-word records by a scroll value and draws each one. Records that pass the upper limit are wrapped by 14500 and have their lateral speeds negated.

name: sync_wait_then_draw_pair
description: Clears a frame counter, calls two routines with the same argument and then two more routines. It then waits until the counter reaches one and calls one final routine.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one routine with no arguments and returns. It is a thin forwarding wrapper with no other work.

name: pop_sorted_entries_above
description: Walks backwards through a list of six-word entries while each entry's first word is at least the argument and the pointer stays inside the list. It calls a routine for each entry it passes and reduces an entry count by six per step.

name: advance_list_until_visible
description: Steps through 12-byte entries while their first word exceeds the argument and a counter is in range. When an entry's vertical value is non-negative and two tests against a routine pass, it adjusts the entry's position by the global offsets and marks it used, returning minus one; otherwise it returns zero.

name: find_next_entry_by_key
description: Scans a six-word table for the first entry whose first word is greater than the argument, within a counted limit. It increments a counter, calls a routine on the found entry and the next one, and returns the entry pointer.

name: write_perspective_entries_table
description: Walks a table of six-word entries and writes three words per entry to an output list: two global values and a scale equal to 25600 divided by the entry's first word plus 600. When the argument is nonzero it also calls another routine for each written entry.

name: update_entry_list_positions
description: Moves each six-word entry by a horizontal step and its velocities, wrapping one coordinate within a range of plus or minus 2048. It then removes entries that have passed a lower bound or have a small vertical value by compacting the list.

name: plot_rotated_point_pairs
description: Scales three matrix values by a per-entry factor and draws six points as offset pairs around a centre. When the argument is non-negative it waits for a frame before each pair, and it advances an accumulator by 288 per point and back by 1440 at the end.

name: advance_level_parameters
description: Derives four parameters from a counter capped at 99: a spacing value equal to the counter plus three capped at ten, a value of two or three, and a value of 15 minus twice the counter. It then calls a routine and increments the counter.

name: examine_undecompiled_routine_b
description: No pseudo-code is available because the decompiler timed out, so this 10-instruction routine's behaviour cannot be stated. It has one caller and one listed callee.

name: plot_word_table_entries
description: Calls an indirect routine with each word of a table in turn, advancing two bytes per word for one more entry than the count in the counter register. It returns the table pointer past the last word.

name: plot_value_pair_via_jumps
description: Passes a word and a long argument to two indirect routines in sequence, one per argument. It is only reached from an unreached gap in the code.

name: call_eleven_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls one routine eleven times in a fixed sequence with no arguments and returns.

name: run_main_action_loop
description: Clears four state variables and runs a loop until a state changes or 1500 frames pass. Each frame it calls a routine with the argument 900, runs several per-frame routines, and lowers a speed value by 250 while it stays above 1000. Afterwards it waits until the state clears and calls a final routine with a stored argument.

name: run_action_frame_loop
description: Runs the per-frame action loop until a state changes or 1500 frames pass. Each frame it calls a routine with the argument 900, lowers a speed value by 250 while it stays above 1000, and increments a counter. Afterwards it waits until the state clears and calls a final routine.

name: wait_until_state_clears
description: Clears a state variable, repeatedly calls a routine until it returns zero, then waits until the state stays zero. It finishes by calling a final routine with a stored argument.

name: draw_dashed_segment_pattern
description: Draws a dashed pattern of point pairs whose length scales with the argument. It plots a fixed opening pair and then loops in steps of 14, emitting paired offsets, with a second loop at an offset of seven.

name: draw_shield_status_panel
description: Draws the shield status display, choosing a bar setting from the shield value: 2 below three, 4 below five, and 1 otherwise. It shows the 'shield gone' text when the shield value is below one and the 'shield' text otherwise, then counts down a counter and draws a fixed bitmap block.

name: adjust_shield_value
description: When a state variable equals one, adds the argument to the shield value and redraws the status. A negative argument with no shield left resets the shield value to minus one and sets two globals to 256 and 15.

name: set_shield_from_parameter
description: Copies the current shield value into a second state variable, sets a timer to ten, adds a word from the argument block to the shield value, and calls a routine to redraw it.

name: dispatch_pause_and_flag_commands
description: Dispatches on a command code: code 64 pauses by waiting for input to clear, drawing the 'Game Paused' text, and resuming on the next input. Code 80 sets one flag to minus one, code 81 clears it, and code 82 inverts a second flag.

name: draw_blinking_status_markers
description: Draws a set of marker shapes at positions taken from a stored x value, using one pattern for state one and an alternating pattern for state three that flips a toggle each call. It then draws two blinking markers driven by counters, offset by 96 on odd counts, and calls another routine.

name: draw_alternating_marker_pattern
description: Draws an alternating marker pattern followed by two blinking counters and a fixed marker shape. It stores the result of a routine in the argument block before returning.

name: draw_marker_shape_at_offset
description: Draws a marker shape at an offset held in a register, then the two blinking counters and a fixed shape at the stored x value. It stores the result of a routine in the argument block.

name: draw_marker_with_counter
description: Draws one marker and one blinking counter, then a fixed shape at the stored x value. It stores the result of a routine in the argument block.

name: draw_fixed_marker_pair
description: Draws a fixed marker shape and then a second fixed shape at the stored x value. It stores the result of a routine in the argument block.

name: update_ship_motion_and_flash
description: Updates two motion values from a target difference, doubling them each frame and clamping them to plus or minus 270 and plus or minus 320. It then smooths two offsets to three quarters of their previous value, and when a flag is set it clears it, toggles a bit and sets a counter to seven.

name: update_motion_offsets_from_block
description: Computes two offsets from a stored value and the difference between two others, then updates the motion values with the same clamping and smoothing as its neighbour. When a flag is set it clears it, toggles a bit and sets a counter to seven.

name: smooth_motion_tail_update
description: Clamps one motion value at 270, doubles and clamps a second at plus or minus 320, and smooths both offsets to three quarters of their previous values. When a flag is set it clears it, toggles a bit and sets a counter to seven.

name: smooth_offsets_and_clear_flag
description: Clamps one motion value at 320, smooths two offsets to three quarters of their previous values, and when a flag is set it clears it, toggles a bit and sets a counter to seven.

name: set_counter_seven_and_call
description: Sets a counter to seven and calls another routine with the argument zero.

name: draw_digits_nibble_by_nibble
description: Draws the digits of a number by extracting one four-bit group at a time, starting from the lowest, and calling a digit routine for each group. The position advances by one step per digit and gains a separator offset every fourth digit.

name: tick_timer_and_draw_banner
description: Decrements a timer and, when it reaches zero, swaps the two display buffer pointers and draws a fixed block at the same position in each buffer. The routine then calls another routine.

name: draw_timed_panel_frame
description: Draws a panel of routines at fixed positions, using argument values read from global data. It then sets a timer to ten and draws a fixed-size block of 15 by 29.

name: draw_counter_indicator_block
description: Draws a fixed-size block of 4 by 11 at a position taken from the screen base, drawing it once when a counter is below ten and twice otherwise.

name: draw_argument_indicator_block
description: Draws a fixed-size block of 17 by 24 at the screen base position, drawing it once when the argument is below ten and twice otherwise.

name: draw_five_offset_markers
description: Computes two scaled values from the differences between pairs of global positions, then calls a routine five times with offsets derived from them. Each call uses a different pair of stored offsets.

name: fill_motion_lookup_tables
description: Advances two accumulators and fills several global words with values from two lookup routines at offsets around a base. It then fills a six-entry table with paired lookups, stepping the accumulator by 288 per entry.

name: draw_decreasing_spacing_row
description: Calls a drawing routine at a fixed second coordinate of 250 for x values starting at 1300. The x value falls by step sizes that shrink from 46 down to 4 as it passes each threshold.

name: draw_glyph_shape_by_code
description: Selects one of several small shape layouts by a numeric code and draws each part through a drawing routine. It updates two stored position values before each part.

name: draw_vector_text_string
description: Draws a null-terminated string one character at a time. Spaces advance the x position by a stored width, and other characters are looked up in a flag table and drawn as stroke shapes through a switch that sets stored position values and calls a drawing routine.

name: read_text_entry_character
description: Polls an input routine up to 30 times until it returns a value in the valid range, then stores the matched character code in a buffer. It then draws the buffer through one of three paths chosen by whether the character is 1, 2 or 3.

name: append_character_to_entry_buffer
description: Appends a character to a short text buffer of up to three characters. Code 3 removes the last character, code 2 adds a space, code 1 stops entry, and a blank code writes a space; input is ignored once the frame counter passes 1500.

name: display_countdown_value_via_routine
description: Computes a display value from a stored counter, using 99 minus it or it minus 100 depending on a flag. It calls a routine with that value and the index 77, then clears the flag and calls another routine with zero if the flag was set.

name: draw_high_score_table
description: Draws a ten-row high score table with a rank, three-character initials and a score on each row, highlighting the row matching the argument. For a new entry it draws the 'insert your initials' prompt, and it also draws the copyright and credit text lines.

name: insert_high_score_entry
description: Sums values from a lookup routine into a score, then inserts it into a ten-entry sorted table, shifting lower entries down. It calls another routine with the new entry afterwards.

name: insert_score_with_shifted_total
description: Accumulates lookup values into a score while shifting a second value right by four bits on each pass. It then inserts the total into the ten-entry sorted table, moving lower entries down, and calls another routine.

name: insert_entry_in_sorted_table
description: Scans the ten-entry table for the first entry the score is at least as large as, moves the entries below it down one place, stores the score there and calls another routine.

name: open_timer_io_request
description: Opens a library and a device, allocates a 56-byte request block, and sends it two commands numbered 9 and 10. It then closes the device and frees the request, calling a routine with zero if an allocation or open fails.

name: clear_global_call_constant
description: Zeroes a global variable and calls another routine with a fixed 24-bit constant as its argument.

name: read_disk_track_sync
description: Configures the disk controller to read a track, then waits for the read-complete flag with a bounded countdown. It scans the track data for the disk sync pattern, counts the words up to the next sync pattern, and if the count is below a minimum it clears a global and calls another routine.

name: reset_level_state_and_hints
description: Resets the level state variables and timers, setting a counter to 750 and a threshold of 15 times the level index (capped at 90) plus 80. When a flag is set it draws the 'Shoot Fireballs' and 'Shoot Tie-Fighters' hint lines.

name: rotate_and_scroll_star_records
description: Moves 31 three-word records toward the viewer by 250 per frame, wrapping them at a lower limit by adding 14500 and negating their lateral speeds. It rotates their lateral positions by two stored offsets and then draws each record.

name: compute_record_lateral_positions
description: Computes two lateral coordinates for a record by calling a lookup routine twice with a 360-unit angle offset. Each result is shifted right by two and stored in the record.

name: spawn_random_record
description: When the active count is below a limit and the speed value exceeds 100, spawns a new 80-byte record. Its position and velocity come from random values, its timer is set to 300, and a free slot in a small table is reserved before the record is drawn.

name: update_active_record_list
description: Decrements five slot timers, then advances every active record by its velocities and runs its timed action. Records that expire are respawned from random values, and a special branch runs when the level count is 20.

name: spawn_enemy_record_from_pool
description: Walks a pool of 80-byte records and, when a random roll and the active count allow, fills one with a random start position and a velocity scaled from its difference to two stored offsets.

name: send_control_word_sequence
description: Issues a fixed sequence of thirteen calls alternating between two indirect routines, then returns the data registers unchanged.

name: draw_polygon_from_record
description: Draws line segments between coordinates read from a record, using a move-then-draw pattern at each vertex. The nine coordinate fields are passed to the drawing routines in turn.

name: draw_record_sprite_parts
description: Draws the parts of a record's sprite according to its flags: up to two parts chosen by a mode flag, then four segments and five points at stored offsets when the last flag is set.

name: update_records_and_check_hits
description: Walks the active record list, moving each record and checking whether it lies inside a horizontal and vertical band. When a random test passes it marks the record, sets a flag and adjusts its timers, then draws each record.

name: remove_one_random_record
description: Scans the record list for the first entry at or above minus 401 with its flag set. When two random tests pass it removes that entry by moving the list tail over it, decrements the count and calls another routine.

name: update_speed_and_score_state
description: Recomputes two timing values from a frame difference and a level counter. When the counter is at least 100 it reduces two accumulators by scaled motion values, and when a flag is set it clears it, toggles a bit, sets a timer to seven and calls another routine.

name: draw_frame_indicator_block
description: Draws a small block at a fixed screen position on each call while a frame counter is below 320, choosing its vertical offset from one bit of a state byte. It does nothing once the counter reaches the limit or the enabling flag is clear.

name: draw_level_progress_indicator
description: Draws a progress indicator from the level counter: below 111 it draws a value derived from the counter minus 60, and otherwise it scales two accumulators and draws the result. It also calls a drawing routine with a fixed frame value.

name: draw_all_record_markers
description: Calls a drawing routine once for each active record, passing that record's stored field and a fixed value of 300.

name: run_level_frame_budget
description: Runs frames while a frame budget counter is non-negative and the state is clear, decrementing the budget each frame and waiting for the frame tick. When the state changes it resets two counters, calls end-of-level routines, clears a flag and returns the state.

name: scale_lookup_to_small_range
description: Calls a lookup routine with its argument, then a second lookup with the fixed value 10000, and returns the second result shifted right by 13 bits.

name: forward_call_no_arguments
description: Calls another routine once with no arguments and returns, doing nothing else.

name: append_point_pair_to_buffer
description: Writes two 32-bit values from its argument into the buffer at the current write pointer and advances the pointer by eight bytes.

name: build_point_table_from_lookups
description: Fills a buffer with 32-bit entries: first pairs of lookup values stepping by 48 up to 1488, then further pairs and a series of entries from a second lookup plus 7500. A block of fixed constants is added through a routine at the end.

name: initialize_star_record_grid
description: Initialises 31 three-word records with a first word starting at minus 259 and rising by 483 per record. The other two words are random values shifted right by 12 bits.

name: pause_after_ten_calls
description: Calls one routine ten times with the same global address, then counts down two million iterations as a delay before returning.

name: load_shape_resources
description: Zeroes the first word of six 22-byte shape entries, then loads six shape files by name: the four laser shapes, the nose shape and the star shape. Each load passes its entry and a global argument.

name: load_named_resource_into_slot
description: Looks up a resource handle from its argument, stores the handle and a word in a table slot, and allocates a block of memory for the resource. It then calls a load routine to fill that block.

name: load_sound_and_shape_assets
description: Loads the sound and shape assets by file name, including the death star, exhaust, hit, laser and missile sounds, several shape files, a pattern file and a music file. It then formats an eight-digit number from a ten-character text buffer, turning blanks into zeros.

name: allocate_game_buffers_and_tables
description: Clears a set of global pointers and sizes, then allocates memory blocks of 32000 bytes (four of them), 4000 bytes, 2600 bytes, three of 1000 bytes, 800 bytes, 32 bytes and 10 bytes. It then fills a 32-byte table with 16-bit values.

name: draw_return_key_prompt
description: Clears the screen, copies an 80-byte block into a buffer, and draws the prompt text 'Return key.' at fixed positions before finishing with a further call.

name: initialize_game_state_variables
description: Sets dozens of global game variables to fixed starting values, including 1024, 300, 360, 100, 160 and 17. It clears a 32-entry table of longs, sets three flags to minus one, and then calls a routine and draws a block of 319 by 30.

name: draw_score_and_wave_labels
description: Resets a flag and two counters, then draws the 'score' and 'wave' labels at fixed positions and a fixed-size block, and finally calls another routine.

name: poll_menu_input_loop
description: Polls a status routine in a loop, calling a dispatch routine while it returns nonzero and another routine while it returns zero. It exits by calling a final routine once the status is zero.

name: load_shape_record_from_file
description: Opens a resource by handle and identifier 1005, reads its ten-byte header, and computes the image size from the header fields. It allocates memory for the pixel data, reads it in, and fills a shape record with dimensions and data pointers; if the resource is missing it calls an error routine.

name: load_shape_with_mask_planes
description: Loads a shape as its neighbour does, then copies each row between end markers of minus one. It also builds three zero-filled companion planes beside it, with each row offset by the stride.

name: blit_clipped_sprite
description: Draws a sprite with the Blitter: it clips the source rectangle against the playfield edges and aligns it to 16-pixel columns. It programs the BLTAPTH, BLTCON0, BLTSIZE and modulo registers and waits on the busy flag between passes, enabling the blitter DMA channels as it goes.

name: load_trumpet_shape_tables
description: Stores twelve fixed 16-bit values and loads the 'shapes/trumpet' resource into newly allocated memory. It builds a five-entry table of offsets and halved sizes from the header, fills three 12-entry tables from a lookup routine, and fills a 120-byte table of values from a second lookup with a zero terminator.

name: parse_chunked_resource_header
description: Reads resource 650 into a buffer, then walks three chunks whose sizes are rounded up to even with an eight-byte header each. It stores the addresses of two chunk data areas and a size word in globals.

name: play_music_stream_step
description: Advances the first music stream on each tick by reading note bytes, choosing periods from a note table and loading the next delay from a lookup. It also writes the DMA control register when a channel starts, and handles the second stream's counter in the same pass.

name: step_audio_channel_zero
description: Advances the stream for audio channel zero: when its note timer expires it selects a period and length from tables, writes the AUD0LCH, AUD0LEN, AUD0PER and AUD0VOL registers, and enables the channel through DMACON. It then reads the next pair of stream bytes and sets the next delay.

name: step_second_music_stream
description: Steps the second music stream: when its timer expires it reads two bytes and, for notes without the high bit set, enables a DMA channel. It then sets the next delay from the note table using the same halving and thirds rules as its neighbour.

name: start_audio_channel_one_note
description: Starts a note on audio channel one by selecting a period from a table and writing the AUD1LCH, AUD1LEN, AUD1PER and AUD1VOL registers. It enables the channel's DMA through DMACON and then sets the next note delay from the note table.

name: refresh_audio_channel_one_pointer
description: When the second stream's delay is below three, writes the channel's address register from a stored base plus 120 and sets its length register to two.

name: initialize_audio_streams
description: Resets the two music stream pointers and their timers, writes the audio volume registers, and sets the DMA control register to enable the channels. It then clears the interrupt enable register and sets the initialised flag.

name: set_state_three_clear_flag
description: Sets a global value to 3 and clears a 16-bit flag. It is entered through a handler pointer in the data hunk.

name: set_flag_one
description: Sets a 16-bit flag to 1 and returns.

name: return_flag_value
description: Returns the current value of a 16-bit flag.

name: dispatch_code_to_routine
description: Dispatches a numeric code: codes 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 19 each call one routine and return its result. Any other code returns the code minus 19.

name: draw_level_bonus_text
description: Resets counters and state for a new run, sets a starting value of 512 and builds a 26-entry table of random positions. It draws the bonus text lines about cleared tower tops and the 50,000 bonus for shooting all towers.

name: update_and_compact_record_table
description: Moves each six-word record by its velocities and applies a random swing to one lateral value. It then removes records whose vertical value has passed a lower limit, compacting the table as it goes.

name: advance_wave_and_spawn_objects
description: Advances the wave counter and scrolls a 51-entry list of positions by a fixed step plus a lateral velocity. It respawns a batch of five entries from a random start, and passes two lists to a routine that orders them before drawing.

name: build_wave_object_lists
description: Fills the object list for five lanes: for each lane it places random positions across the screen, records an object type and an encoded value, and sets each object's weight. The weight is 700 early in the wave and falls off with the wave timer after that.

name: draw_wave_object_by_type
description: Draws a wave object according to its type code. Types 1 and 2 each use their own sequence of plotted points and fill calls from the object's coordinate fields, and the other types use a further set of routines. It is the largest per-object drawing routine.

name: spawn_shots_from_wave_objects
description: For each unflagged wave object of type 1 or 2, rolls a random number and sometimes spawns a shot record with a speed of 15000 or minus 3000. The shot copies the object's coordinates and its record is linked back to the source object, which is then flagged.

name: check_player_object_collisions
description: Checks each active object against the player's position for a hit. When an object falls inside its bounds the player's state changes to hit and a sound effect is played, and the routine also counts down the shots and draws the surviving objects.

name: remove_objects_entering_range
description: Removes the first active object lying in a small horizontal band when a random test passes, and sets a 16-frame timer. It then checks the remaining objects for a close approach and, when one is found, sets a flag and a negative timer.

name: update_camera_offset_lookup
description: Updates a stored offset and a step value from a 32-bit counter, using a lookup routine to decide when to reverse direction. It then stores two scaled values from further lookups for later use.

name: update_pitch_state_and_timer
description: Recomputes two motion values from the frame difference and random limits derived from the wave counter, then updates a smoothed value. When a flag is set it clears it, toggles a bit, sets a counter to seven and calls another routine.

name: draw_player_shot_indicator
description: Draws the player's shot marker at one of three horizontal offsets chosen from flags and the shot counter, then advances the counter. On alternate counts it also draws a block at a fixed offset.

name: update_wave_frame_display
description: Updates the wave display for one frame by passing a list pointer to two routines. For later waves while the wave counter is under 500 and no flag is set it makes an extra pair of routine calls, then finishes with a final call.

name: run_descent_scroll_until_position
description: Returns zero on the first level. Otherwise it scrolls 50 three-word entries by a fixed step each frame until a position drops to 5000, drawing each frame and adjusting a speed value, then returns the status word.

name: project_point_by_depth
description: Divides two 32-bit coordinates by a depth value offset by 470, and again by a second depth offset of 730, to produce two projected screen coordinates. Each pair is stored in globals.

name: project_offset_pair_by_depth
description: Projects two horizontal offsets of minus and plus 30720 by dividing each by a depth value offset by 470, then again by 730. It stores the four projected values in globals.

name: project_three_values_two_depths
description: Projects three 32-bit values by dividing each by a depth offset of 450 and again by 750, storing six scaled results in globals.

name: project_pair_and_single_value
description: Projects a pair of offsets of minus and plus 46080 divided by a depth offset of 750, and a single value divided by a depth offset of 450. It stores the three results in globals.

name: draw_level_hint_text
description: Draws the in-level text, choosing a hint line by the level index from 'Points for using the FORCE', 'EXHAUST PORT AHEAD', 'EXHAUST PORT MISSED', 'avoid catwalks', 'shoot fireballs' and 'use the force'. It then fills position tables for the level.

name: initialize_wave_position_tables
description: Clears timers and counters, sets the wave counter to 129 and the speed to 500. It then fills two 11-entry tables with positions starting at 1 and rising by 1900, with the second table offset by 950.

name: scroll_wave_position_ring
description: Computes three projection bases from the speed value times 512 and plus or minus 153600, then scrolls an 11-entry ring of positions. When the first entry passes minus 589 the ring rotates, the wave counter drops by one, and a routine is called when the counter reaches 8.

name: draw_table_rows_by_argument
description: Draws a run of rows taken from a 16-point table. Below an argument of two it runs seven rows from the given row, and otherwise it runs twenty rows back from it, drawing each row's points through two routines.

name: run_bonus_tally_screen
description: Runs the end-of-level bonus screen: it draws the star field and the shield number, then loops over frames while counting bonus points for remaining shields. The text lines 'Death Star destroyed', 'Starting Bonus Points', 'Shield at full Strength', '1 added to Shield Strength' and 'Bonus for remaining Shields' are drawn at fixed positions.

name: draw_masked_glyph_bits
description: Uses the bits of its argument to choose drawing actions: for each of four nibbles it calls one routine when the low two bits are set and another when the next two are set, then returns the last result. It also records a hit when two comparisons on stored positions both match.

name: draw_shape_by_selector
description: Draws one of three point sequences chosen by a selector value. Selector 12 draws an eleven-point sequence, selector 8 draws an eight-point sequence, and any other value draws the default eight-point sequence, with the points read from stored coordinate globals.

name: draw_bit_pattern_row
description: Walks the four nibbles of a 16-bit pattern and draws a row of cells, advancing the offset by 26624 each step. Each nibble draws one or two cells depending on its bits, and the routine returns the last cell's result.

name: copy_view_values_and_call
description: Calls a routine with a stored value, copies four view values into an eight-word table, then calls another routine with a value from the wave table. Once the wave counter reaches nine that value is the fixed 18400.

name: process_fire_input_and_shots
description: Checks the fire bit pattern from the input record and, when no cooldown is active and the nearest entry is clear, tries to fire up to five shots. Each shot is created when a random value is under 125 and its lateral position is in range, then a cooldown is set.

name: draw_wave_clear_sequence
description: Draws the end-of-wave sequence when the current wave's value is positive: it draws a block of marker shapes at fixed positions, lowers a counter by 250, and draws the remaining scene elements through several drawing routines.

name: advance_entries_below_key
description: Walks the entry list backwards while the current entry's first word is below the argument and the pointer stays inside the list. It calls a routine for each entry it passes and steps the list pointers.

name: spawn_objects_from_mask
description: When the wave allows it, reads a bit mask from the current table entry and rolls a random value for each set bit. Successful rolls add an object record at the next table slot with a start position and a vertical speed taken from a stored value.

name: draw_status_icons_by_wave
description: Draws status icons according to the wave counter: before wave eight, or with the flag clear, it draws one icon at a base offset; otherwise it draws at a different offset. A blink counter decides whether a second icon is drawn, and after wave 120 further icons are drawn.

name: draw_player_ship_and_shots
description: Draws the player's ship as plotted points around its stored position, after first adjusting a stored value by minus 130. It then plots the shots from the table with a second set of points and advances the table, drawing extra shapes once the wave counter reaches nine.

name: draw_animated_point_frame
description: Builds two sets of coordinate points offset by plus and minus 130 from a stored value, then plots the stored points of a figure as move-and-draw pairs. Part of the buffer is generated from the stored values before the drawing loop runs.

name: run_angle_sweep_frames
description: Runs a frame loop that sweeps an angle from minus 720 up to zero, advancing by 40 per frame and by 20 and then 12 once the sweep passes minus 360 and minus 120. Each step sets a random-driven offset, draws a frame and waits for the frame tick.

name: wait_frames_until_event
description: Runs frames while neither of two flags is set, drawing each frame and waiting for the frame tick. When the loop ends it sets the state flags from the wave counter and, if the flag is clear, sets a final flag to minus one.

name: run_title_loop_until_flag
description: Loops over frames while two flags stay clear, alternating which message is drawn according to the level index. It then clears a pending flag and returns the first flag.

name: return_global_block_address
description: Returns the address of a fixed offset within the global data block without reading or writing it.

name: call_library_function_minus_30
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 30 from a base held in a register, with no arguments. The jump table could not be recovered, so the target function is unknown.

name: open_dos_library_and_start
description: Clears a block of longwords of global storage and saves the task pointer. It opens dos.library by name through the exec library, raising an alert when the library is missing and otherwise handing control to the main routine.

name: stub_return_no_action
description: Does nothing and returns immediately. It has one caller.

name: allocate_entry_list_files
description: Allocates a six-byte-per-entry block for an entry list, fills in its fields and writes the four-letter marker 'MANX' into it. It then opens files through the DOS wrappers for current directory, input, output and open, loads resource 1005 and calls a routine.

name: parse_text_file_tokens
description: Splits a text buffer into tokens: whitespace is skipped, double-quoted strings are copied with doubled quotes read as one, and other tokens end at a space, tab, newline or null. Each token is stored in a table, and allocation and library routines set up the buffer first.

name: copy_string_pad_zeros
description: Copies bytes from a source to a destination up to a count or until a null terminator is found, then fills any remaining bytes of the count with zeros.

name: copy_string_pad_zeros
description: Copies bytes from a source to a destination up to a count or until a null terminator is found, then fills any remaining bytes of the count with zeros. The code is identical to the routine at the previous address.

name: append_string_bounded
description: Appends a source string to the end of a destination string, copying up to about 32767 characters and writing a terminating zero when the source ends first. The code is entered only from an unreached gap.

name: append_string_with_limit
description: Walks to the end of the destination string, then copies the source string into it until the source's terminating zero or until a count from the third argument runs out. If the count runs out first, a terminating zero is written after the copied bytes.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a source pointer to a destination pointer until a zero byte is copied, including the terminator. It returns the original destination pointer.

name: compute_cross_product_halves
description: Computes the cross terms of the 16-bit halves of two 32-bit register inputs and combines them into the upper longword of a 64-bit result. The second input is returned unchanged in the lower longword, so this is not a full 32-bit multiply.

name: open_icon_library_for_window
description: Opens icon.library by name, finds a window-related structure through a library call, and loads resource 1005 into a field of the window record. It then closes the library through the library call vectors at offsets minus 78, minus 90 and minus 96.

name: format_string_into_buffer
description: Stores a destination pointer, passes the argument list on the stack to a formatting routine, and then clears the first byte of the destination buffer. It returns the formatting routine's result.

name: format_string_return_word
description: Stores a destination pointer, passes the argument list on the stack to a formatting routine, clears the first byte of the destination, and returns the formatting result as a word.

name: store_byte_and_advance_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of its argument to the global destination pointer, advances that pointer by one and returns the byte. It serves as the output step for a formatting routine.

name: forward_format_call
description: Passes its argument and the stack argument block to a formatting routine together with a callback, and returns nothing.

name: examine_undecompiled_routine_c
description: The decompiler timed out, so no pseudo-code is available for this 48-instruction routine. It has one caller and two listed callees, so its behaviour cannot be stated from the evidence.
